preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and isinstance(y, int) for x, y in [(n, m)])
preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n and m representing the grid dimensions.
Grid dimensions n and m are within the range [1, 100].

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == ['k'] + [f'{x} {y}' for x, y in points]
postconditions.description: Output consists of an integer k (the size of the beautiful set) followed by k lines, each containing two integers representing the coordinates of a point in the set.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= n and 0 <= y <= m and x + y > 0 for x, y in points)
postconditions.description: All points in the output set lie within the grid bounds and satisfy x + y > 0.
The integer k matches the number of points in the output set.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(distance_squared(p1, p2), float) and not distance_squared(p1, p2).is_integer() for p1 in points for p2 in points if p1 != p2)
postconditions.description: For any two distinct points in the set, the squared distance between them is non-integer, ensuring the distance is non-integer.

postconditions.expression: not any(all(distance_squared(p1, p2).is_integer() for p2 in points if p2 != p1) for p1 in points)
postconditions.description: No point in the set has an integer distance to all other points in the set.
The size k of the output set is the maximum possible for the given grid dimensions.
